From first sketch to the keys
settings.intro: Every project starts with a conversation on site. Here is what happens after that.

settings.text: Why small buildings

Small buildings are where design matters most. Every square metre has a job, every window frames something, and there is nowhere for a bad decision to hide.

We started Meridian to work at that scale: close to the people who will live in the rooms, and close to the builders who make them.
The net store, slowly
The building had stood empty for eleven years. Salt had eaten the window frames and the roof leaked in four places, but the walls were good: half a metre of local stone.

image.alt: Stone walls and a new timber roof under construction

settings.caption: The new roof going on, March 2025.

settings.text: We kept everything the sea had not already taken.
Inside, a single oak stair connects the studio to the flats above, lit from a long rooflight that follows the ridge.

settings.question: How much does an architect cost?
settings.answer: For most of our projects, between 8 and 12 percent of the build cost. We agree a fixed fee before we start.

settings.question: Do you work outside Portwell?
settings.answer: Yes, anywhere within about two hours. Further than that, we will recommend someone local.

settings.question: How long does planning take?
settings.answer: Usually eight to thirteen weeks from submission. We will tell you early if a site looks difficult.

settings.question: Can you work with my builder?
settings.answer: Of course. We are happy to tender too, if you would like to compare.

settings.text: A house that fits its site
We start with the land: the light, the wind, the view you will want from the kitchen sink. Most of our houses are timber-framed and built by local firms.
More room, same house
A good extension makes the old house work better, not just bigger. We often find the space is already there.
Small shops and studios

settings.title: Ana Ferreira
settings.text:
Ana grew up two streets from the studio and trained in Lisbon and London. Before Meridian she spent eight years on housing schemes for a large practice, and came home wanting to build smaller, better.

She leads every house project from the first visit to handover, and still answers the studio phone on Mondays.
